accepted.question_text: Let f(n) denote the number of 1-factors (perfect matchings) of the n-dimensional cube. The paper reports a simple proof of the parity statement that f(n) has the same parity as n, and then states that similar but more complex reasoning should allow one to compute the enumerating sequence modulo any power of 2. Determine, in a self-contained explicit form, the value of f(n) modulo 2^m for arbitrary m ≥ 1.
accepted.context_brief: Perfect matchings of the n-cube modulo powers of 2

trace.notes: Mapped the PDF as a four-page progress report organized by Problem 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 10, 14, 15, 16, 18, and 19. No internal theorem/proposition list was found; the document mostly reports solved status and follow-up references.

Extracted Problem 1 and Problem 2 update text on page 1. Problem 1 contains a remaining proof-simplicity challenge; Problem 2 only reports a solved enumeration result without restating the original problem.
Extracted page-2 problem updates. Problems 3 and 4 are reported as solved; Problem 6 points to an interpretation of KK* but does not restate the original open problem.
Extracted page-3 problem updates. Problems 8, 9, and 10 are solved-status entries; Problem 14 reports polynomial bounds and exact polynomiality for fixed width.
Extracted page-4 problem updates. Problems 15 and 16 are solved-status entries, Problem 18 gives a response reference, and Problem 19 explicitly suggests a remaining modulo-2^m computation question.

Rewrote the remaining Problem 19 direction into a standalone question by inlining the definition of f(n) as the number of 1-factors in the n-cube and preserving the modulo-any-power-of-2 goal stated in the paper.

Could not make Problem 1 fully self-contained because the quoted text mentions the answer "one-third" and a special case that solves Problem 1, but does not state the original problem precisely enough to support a standalone rewrite without adding unsupported facts.
No near-duplicate rewritten questions were found among the extracted candidates.

Accepted only the Problem 19 modulo-2^m item because it passed self-containedness and evidence coverage. The remaining problem-number entries were moved to needs_review because the progress report reports status or references without enough quoted context to reconstruct the original problems safely.
